comments.text:
I was an Air Force Aircraft mechanic and reviewed a lot of aircraft crashes.   

Mechanically, the rapid descent after a sharp turn is likely indicative of a sudden loss of lift or an issue with flight controls.  

In order of what I would imagine being most likely.
-pilot attempted to show off.  The people on that flight were not normal people to have on the flight deck and are exactly the type of people a pilot would want to show off to.  See the Elmendorf 2010 C-17 Crash 

-Wing Root Snapped. It's a B-52, the airframe is old.  We do Isochronal and other depot level maintenance on Aircraft like this and C-5 including X-raying the frame but it's still degraded over time and human's are imperfect. See the 2012 C-130H3 Crash

-Loss of Flight Controls due to mechanical defect

-Pilot Error.  See Dover C5 Galaxy 2006 Crash and many commercial flight losses.

-Very unlikely, but with precedent.  Pilot intentionally crashed.
